sections.content: How many people are "sales and retail assistants"?

1,114,355 people

were counted on the census as "sales and retail assistants" in England and Wales in March 2021.

This makes this type of work the most common occupation reported on the census.

Sales and retail assistants demonstrate and sell a variety of goods and services in shops, stores, showrooms and similar establishments.

People who had this job were generally younger

The occupation of "sales and retail assistants" had a younger age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 20 to 24 years. Of the whole working population 7.9% were aged 20 to 24 years. For people working as "sales and retail assistants", 18.3% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "sales and retail assistants" was 65 years or older.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "sales and retail assistants" included:

  • elementary sales occupations (other)
  • kitchen and catering assistants
  • shelf fillers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "sales and retail assistants" there were more women than men (63.9% compared with 36.1%).

This means "sales and retail assistants" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "sales occupations".

Men made up 36.1% and women made up 63.9% of "sales and retail assistants"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "sales and retail assistants" included:

  • medical and dental technicians
  • pharmacists
  • call and contact centre occupations

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "sales and retail assistants" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of women with this occupation than men.

The percentage of men and women who are "sales and retail assistants" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "sales and retail assistants", 12.3% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a younger age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work part-time than full-time (71% compared with 29%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (96.9%) than self-employed (3.1%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
